% 01.12.2025 CRL.M.A. 35720/2025 (under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 for Early Hearing)
1. An Application has been filed on behalf of the Petitioners seeking early hearing.

2. It is submitted that the matter has been duly compromised and they have a fundamental right of expeditious disposal of the matters and, therefore, a prayer is made that the matter may be taken up today as the parties are present.
3. The Application is allowed subject to payment of cost of Rs.10,000/- each to be paid by both the parties with the Delhi High Court Advocates' Welfare Trust, within five days.
4. The Application stands disposed of.
This is a digitally signed order.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that the marriage was solemnized between petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 on 06.08.2021 according to Sikh rites and ceremonies.
It is stated that on 26.07.2022 one child namely Jasleen Kaur was born out of the said wedlock.
Due to certain differences and disputes between Petitioner No.1 and Respondent No.2 they started residing separately.

7. It is further submitted that on 06.06.2022, on the complaint of respondent No. 2 made before CAW Cell, an FIR bearing No. 0276/2023 under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 got registered at Police Station Gulabi Bagh.

8. It is stated that during the trial of the matter, the case was referred to Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari District Courts, Delhi, where both the parties amicably settled all the disputes and differences before Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari District Courts, Delhi vide Compromise Deed dated 08.04.2025, and it was inter alia settled between the parties that the respondent No. 2/wife and the petitioner No. 1/husband shall dissolve their marriage by decree of mutual consent.
It is stated that petitioner No. 1/husband shall pay a sum of Rs. 35,00,000/- to the respondent No. 2/wife towards full and final amount of all the claims of the respondent No. 2/wife.

It is also stated that the petitioner No. 1 has already paid Rs.23,00,000 to respondent No. 2/wife in three instalments viz.,

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 02/12/2025 at 21:32:31 11,00,000/- was paid at the time of recording of statements in First Motion Petition under Section 13(b) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and another Rs.11,00,000/- was paid at the time of recording of statements in Second Motion Petition under Section 13(b)(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
9. It is further stated that the remaining third instalment of Rs.12,00,000/- shall be paid by the petitioner No. 1/husband at the time of quashing of FIR No.0276/2023.
It is also stated that the child shall remain in the custody of respondent No. 2/wife and the Petitioner No.1/husband shall have no visitation rights.
10. It is also stated that on 26.07.2025, the marriage between petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 had been dissolved as per Hindu law.
11. In view of the Compromise Deed dated 08.04.2025, the present Petition has been filed.
12. The parties are present before this Court in-person today, and have been identified by their counsel and Investigating Officer concerned.
The parties have endorsed the amicable settlement and accepted the terms thereof voluntarily.
It is stated that the accused Harinder Singh has died on 27.02.2025 and his Death Certificate has been submitted.

sentences.text: The balance amount of Rs.12,00,000/- has been paid to the respondent No. 2/wife by the petitioner No. 1 today in the Court.

Out of total balance amount of Rs.12,00,000/-, Rs.7,00,000/-
has been paid as DD No."001405" dated 14.11.2025 drawn on HDFC Bank in the name of Respondent No.2 and an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- has been paid through LIC Policies No."0364033", "0364041" and "0364263" in the name of minor daughter namely Jasleen Kaur, and the same has been confirmed by the respondent No. 2/wife.
This is a digitally signed order.

The parties have submitted that all the disputes have been amicably settled vide Compromise Deed dated 08.04.2025 and thus, no fruitful purpose will be served in continuing with the FIR.
15. The present petition has been signed by all the parties and is supported by their respective affidavits.

The parties have reaffirmed the terms of the settlement arrived at vide Compromise Deed dated 08.04.2025 and they also submit that the said Compromise Deed has been arrived at between the parties without any pressure and coercion.
16. Today, the complainant/respondent No. 2/wife, who is present in Court, states that she has received all amounts due to her and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

17. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will and without any coercion and also the fact that the present matter is a family matter, I am of the opinion that no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
18. Moreover, there is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

19. Accordingly, FIR bearing No. 0276/2023 registered at Police Station Gulabi Bagh, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
20. It is made clear that the above Settlement is without prejudice to the rights of the child.
